question: By weight, what share of the pesticides in a typical American diet did Ames estimate plants make themselves?
answer: About 99.99%. Plants cannot run, so they make chemical defences against insects and fungi, in cabbage, coffee, celery and more. Ames and colleagues estimated Americans eat about 1,500 mg of these a day, some 10,000 times more than synthetic pesticide residues. Natural chemicals get no exemption from toxicology; the dose decides.
move: Judge a substance by its dose, not by where it came from.
ask: Do I trust something more because it is labelled natural, without asking how much I take?
trap: Pesticides are factory chemicals, so most must come from farm sprays.
reference: Ames, Profet & Gold, Dietary pesticides (99.99% all natural), Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 1990
